output:
Dear everyone,

I’ve just finished a run of nights and have been catching up. First, I’m genuinely thrilled that Amma and Appa are coming to Leicester. Anika has already made them a laminated welcome timetable, including “Paati teaches us rasam, Tuesdays,” and Rohan is looking forward to showing Appa the vegetable patch properly.

Kiran, you’re right that I should have spoken to you earlier. I started the visa paperwork because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, but I should have looped you in then. I’m sorry I didn’t. I don’t want to brush past that or make you feel your concerns are being managed rather than heard.

On Appa’s heart: the visa is the UK long-term visitor one, allowing up to six months per visit. The plan is to come in the first week of April and return at the end of September 2027. I’ve got a travel-insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover for about £640 each for the six months; the agent says it covers the stent. Dr. Prakash has agreed to review Appa in March before they fly and do a video consultation in July, and he’s happy to share his notes with me. Leicester Royal is 15 minutes from our house, and I know half the cardiology team. I’ll make sure we have the policy details and medical notes to hand, and we can talk through any remaining questions together before they travel.

Amma’s six-week limit is fair to raise, especially as she hasn’t been away from home for this long. She can go home whenever she wants, and the return ticket will be flexible. I don’t want anyone to feel committed to staying the full six months if it doesn’t suit them.

And Ganesh Chaturthi shouldn’t have to disappear from the plan. Amma and Appa could fly from Leicester to Pune in September and finish their trip there, or the Pune family could come to Leicester in August. I’d be very happy to cover your flights for an August visit.

One thing I want to clarify for everyone: this idea came from Appa, not from me. When Rohan showed him the vegetable patch on video in August, Appa said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” I took that as the beginning of a conversation, but I can see I should have made sure we all had that conversation together before taking steps on the paperwork.

Would a family video call this Sunday work, at 4pm UK / 9.30pm India? We can talk it all through, including what would make the visit comfortable for Amma and Appa and what works for Pune. I’m excited to have them here, and I want us to make the plan together.

Love,
Meera
